subject: MSA/addendum sync — capacity uptick & term reconciliation for Stratus Media
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusmedia.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + expansion: term length, +3 GPU units, and MSLA changes

Thanks Vanessa / Jonas —

Per our exec discussion this morning, Stratus Media is ready to move forward with the renewal but we need to reconcile a few legal and commercial points before procurement can raise a PO:

- Term: we'd like to move from a 12-month renewal to a 24-month committed term.
- Capacity: add 3 dedicated GPU units (total would become 5) for steady-state throughput through H1.
- Data residency: we need a tighter residency clause for EU customer data routed to our accounts (we expect some European traffic).
- Termination / exit: procurement is flagging the 60-day termination-for-convenience notice — they want it extended to 90 days or a pro-rata buyout option.

Can you send an updated order form and the MSLA with proposed redlines? If you can include an estimate for the month-to-month overage cost during the transition that helps procurement model spend.

I've cc'd procurement@stratusmedia.com (they will be the PO owner). Happy to set a quick call if that helps — next available window is Thurs 11/19 afternoon PT.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, AI Platforms
Stratus Media

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Draft redlines + provisional pricing for capacity uplift

Elaine / Vanessa —

Following up from Vanessa's note, attached are two documents: Redwood_MSLA_v3_redlines.pdf and OrderForm_Stratus_Expansion_v2.xlsx. Quick summary of the material redlines and commercial points we've included so procurement can review:

- Term: MSLA redline reflects the 24-month commitment with an auto-renewal checkbox removed; renewal will require explicit PO or written consent.
- Capacity & pricing: Order form shows pricing for +3 dedicated GPUs (line item includes per-GPU hourly rate, monthly committed spend, and a migration credit for the first two months to aid cutover).
- Data residency: proposed clause narrows residency requirement to "Customer EU-origin data" and specifies that Redwood will route EU stay-in-region where technically feasible; we added a quarterly audit right and SOC 2 reference.
- Termination: we've proposed a 90-day notice for termination for convenience OR a pro-rata buyout calculated on remaining committed months. We note that a buyout will accelerate invoicing for committed capacity.
- SLA credits: clarified crediting mechanism and cap for multi-region failover scenarios.

Attachments: Redwood_MSLA_v3_redlines.pdf (annotated), OrderForm_Stratus_Expansion_v2.xlsx (pricing), short pricing summary in body below.

Provisional commercial (monthly):
- 5 dedicated GPUs (committed): $68,000 / month (includes 10% committed discount vs on-demand)
- Migration/transition credit: $10,000 applied across 2 months post effective date
- Implementation services estimate (if needed): $6,500 one-time for onboarding assistance

Open items we flagged for your procurement: billing cutoff dates for the first partial month, and whether Stratus requires invoice-level PO numbers (we can support).

If this looks generally aligned I can push the redlines to our contracts team and generate a DocuSign envelope for signature once procurement confirms the PO timing.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0223

Elaine / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Jonas. I reviewed the redlines and had two suggested edits from contracts/finance to keep the deal close and procurement-friendly:

1) Termination-for-convenience: accept the 90-day notice option, but add express language that any pro-rata buyout amount will be capped at 60% of the remaining committed value to avoid immediate full acceleration. This is a standard compromise we can live with for enterprise renewals.

2) Data residency: we'll accept the "Customer EU-origin data" routing approach, provided Stratus agrees to an operational tolerance clause (i.e., "where technically feasible") and a 30-day remediation window for any cross-region routing incidents.

Next steps from our side: I'll prepare a DocuSign envelope once procurement confirms the PO template fields (we've attached a Stratus PO template below for your convenience). If procurement prefers Redwood to create the PO we can generate a PO-ready invoice but we usually wait for buyer-signed PO.

DocuSign link and envelope details will follow — I can also flip the package to a sign-first model if Stratus wants signature to precede PO issuance.

Regards,
